module.mta_sts.checks: Downloads the domain's MTA-STS policy, validates it (version, mode, max age, content type), compares its mx: patterns with the real MX hosts and details TLS-RPT (report destinations).
module.mta_sts.fix:
First, check that every MX server offers STARTTLS with a valid certificate for the MX name: `openssl s_client -starttls smtp -connect mx1.example.com:25 -servername mx1.example.com`. In `enforce` mode, an MX without a valid certificate stops receiving mail.
Create the name `mta-sts.example.com` (A, AAAA or CNAME record) pointing to a web server with HTTPS and a valid certificate for that name.
Publish the file `/.well-known/mta-sts.txt` there, served as `text/plain` without redirection, with `version: STSv1`, `mode: testing`, one `mx:` line per real MX server (a pattern such as `*.example.net` is accepted) and `max_age`.
Publish the TXT record `_mta-sts.example.com`: `v=STSv1; id=` followed by an alphanumeric identifier (for example the date). Change the `id` every time the policy changes, otherwise senders keep the old one.
Publish TLS-RPT in a TXT record `_smtp._tls.example.com` (`v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@example.com`) to receive encryption failure reports.
After 2 to 4 weeks of reports without failures, replace `testing` with `enforce`, set `max_age` to at least 604800 (one week), then change the `id`.
Unusable policy or uncovered MX: make the `mx:` lines match the current MX hosts (`dig +short MX example.com`); the policy host must resolve and answer HTTP 200 without redirection. Whenever you change MX, update the policy before the change.
Check with `curl -i https://mta-sts.example.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt` and `dig +short TXT _mta-sts.example.com`, then run the scan again. A domain that receives no mail does not need MTA-STS.
module.mta_sts.fix_snippet:
# DNS
mta-sts.example.com.  IN  A  203.0.113.10
_mta-sts.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=STSv1; id=20261015T000000"
_smtp._tls.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@example.com"
# mta-sts.txt
version: STSv1
mode: testing
mx: mx1.example.com
mx: mx2.example.com
max_age: 604800
# curl
curl -i https://mta-sts.example.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt
module.mta_sts.title: MTA-STS and TLS-RPT
module.mta_sts.why: MTA-STS forces sending servers to encrypt mail to your MX hosts: without it, a network attacker can downgrade delivery to plaintext. A policy that misses an MX also blocks legitimate mail.
